record.name: Turkey
record.summary: No qualifying institute or commitment identified. Action 16 of the 2026-2030 plan strengthens TÜBİTAK BİLGEM AI Institute capacity for AI safety and performance evaluation and requires high-impact systems to be tested before deployment and major updates.

related_bodies.name: TÜBİTAK BİLGEM Artificial Intelligence Institute
related_bodies.role: Its tests cover security, performance, robustness, bias, explainability, data protection and cyber resistance. Pre-deployment and major-update testing applies to high-impact systems defined by sensitive uses. It is an existing public AI institute whose general AI safety-assessment capacity is strengthened by action 16. A national general-purpose/frontier capability or behaviour-risk evaluation remit remains unresolved.

related_bodies.name: Cybersecurity Presidency (Siber Güvenlik Başkanlığı)
related_bodies.role: It coordinates technical safety assessment alongside existing public bodies; participation in the action plan is not designation of an AISI.

related_bodies.name: National AI Ethics Board (planned in action 4)
related_bodies.role: It would provide guidance, ethical assessment and referral of submissions. Binding supervision would remain with sectoral regulators. No designation to evaluate advanced models was found.

next_check.reason: Clarify the AI Institute's national remit to test advanced models for capabilities or behaviour risks in action 16 implementation documents.

check.language_note: The recorded tr queries use a national or official language selected for this country-specific check. Other national or official languages were not exhaustively searched. Search source_ids identify registered source URLs matched in the retrieved result set, which may include irrelevant hits. An empty list means no registered source URL was matched, not that the web response was empty. The earlier audit used independent_source_ids for substantive corroboration; governance_source_ids, where present, identifies the selected primary governance evidence. The earlier English-search pass on 17 October 2026 left the then-recorded national or official-language coverage unchanged; the work is described below. The additional status review recorded Turkish and English searches and read the Turkish plan and parliamentary inquiry plus the institute's English description. The final two queries in the additional status review shared the same search request. Their source_ids record the common matched URL, not attribution to either individual query. Search batches for the additional status review, using 1-based positions in check.searches: 4, 5, 6; 7, 8, 9; 10, 11. Each group records the same exact registered URLs found in its combined search results, without attribution to an individual query. Explicit page opens and finds and unverified URL variants are excluded. Groups list the recorded queries; some requests also contained additional queries retained in the research evidence.
check.independence_note: Historical audit under the superseded two-independent-sources rule: Two substantively independent evidence origins were not established. Multiple pages from one owner, mirrors, reports of the same underlying announcement and general regional coverage are not counted as independent corroboration.
check.governance_note: The ministry plan strengthens safety-assessment capacity within the existing AI institute; its detailed high-impact definition concerns sensitive uses. The complete inquiry recommendation table proposes governance and deployment-related tests without naming a qualifying institute. The report attributes the inquiry's creation and member selection to Parliament; its background chapters were not read in full. None of these sources resolves the mandate covering advanced models.

record.notes: Actions 4 and 16 were re-read in the ministry plan's Alomaliye-hosted copy, at PDF pages 25 and 35 (printed pages 16 and 26). Action 16 strengthens safety-evaluation capacity within TÜBİTAK BİLGEM AI Institute, covering test methods, tools and guides for security, performance, robustness, bias, explainability, data protection and cyber resistance. It separately requires high-impact systems to be evaluated against these criteria before deployment and major updates, without naming the evaluator in that sentence. Action 4 defines high-impact systems through sensitive uses such as health, education, employment, credit, biometrics and policing. This supports deployment assurance but does not resolve a national remit to evaluate general-purpose or frontier models for capabilities or behaviour risks. The institute's English website describes core technology development and links between research and industry. The March 2026 parliamentary inquiry report recommends a broad AI governance authority (19), independent audits (42) and pre-use tests of models and systems for national-security risks, especially in critical infrastructure (47). Recommendation 47 includes misuse scenarios and cyber vulnerabilities, but names no institute. The final audit reviewed all 100 recommendations, at printed pages 768–783, and found no proposal for a qualifying institute to evaluate advanced models. The formation account at printed pages 24 and 26 attributes creation and member selection to Parliament. The background chapters were not read in full. Turkish and English searches did not identify a later qualifying designation. A fresh request for the ministry-hosted plan returned Request Rejected, and one attempt to retrieve a text copy failed. The previously preserved official PDF remains a separate historical retrieval; the substantive third-party copy was used and did not compare its bytes with the official snapshot. The earlier review of the summit announcement, Gazette circular metadata and CMS explanation remains part of the source history; those records do not resolve the technical remit.
